intro.what.mathematics: An infinity-category is introduced informally through objects, arrows and higher arrows, with weakly coherent composition. This introductory description is not a complete formal definition.
intro.what.proof: No proof-bearing formal definition is asserted in this introductory passage.
intro.what.plain: The opening motivates a setting in which relations between maps are themselves part of the structure.
intro.what.story: Mira's route book now records comparisons between permits and comparisons between those comparisons, without declaring a final formal charter.
intro.what.limit: The picture is motivation. An ordinary Lean category does not encode the full higher structure.

intro.higher_morphisms.mathematics: The introductory hierarchy consists of objects, morphisms between objects, 2-morphisms between parallel morphisms, and higher morphisms between parallel morphisms of the preceding dimension.
intro.higher_morphisms.proof: This is an informal description of dimensions, not a completed axiom system.
intro.higher_morphisms.plain: At each level, comparisons have endpoints at the previous level.
intro.higher_morphisms.story: Mira compares two permits with the same endpoints, then compares two such comparisons, and continues the ledger to higher levels.
intro.higher_morphisms.limit: No finite tower of ordinary arrows is claimed to formalize all dimensions.

intro.invertibility.mathematics: In the intended infinity-category setting, k-morphisms for k≥2 are invertible in a weak sense, and units and associativity hold through compatible higher identifications.
intro.invertibility.proof: The exact weak structures and their axioms are deferred in the source.
intro.invertibility.plain: Higher identifications replace some strict equations, but those identifications must themselves fit together.
intro.invertibility.story: Mira allows regrouping certificates rather than identical route entries, and then requires certificates comparing the different ways of using those certificates.
intro.invertibility.limit: Lean's proof-irrelevant equality does not provide the intended higher identity structure; no ordinary analogue is a proof of this synthetic claim.
obligations: Represent the stated all-dimensional weak coherence in the intended foundations

intro.paths.mathematics: For a topological space, points, paths, endpoint-fixing homotopies and higher boundary-fixing homotopies motivate the fundamental infinity-groupoid. Path concatenation is associative and unital up to homotopy; reversal is an inverse up to homotopy.
intro.paths.proof: The source sketches the construction. The one-dimensional homotopy laws have ordinary topological formalizations; the full infinite construction requires a precise higher model.
intro.paths.plain: Concatenating parameterized paths in different groupings changes the parameterization, but a homotopy relates the results.
intro.paths.story: Mira redraws journeys continuously while keeping the endpoints fixed. A journey out and back can be contracted, and different timing conventions can be deformed into one another.
intro.paths.limit: A homotopy is a specified continuous deformation. This does not make the parameterized paths literally equal or formalize all higher coherence.
obligations: Path concatenation associativity up to endpoint-fixed homotopy
Left and right path identities up to homotopy
Path reversal gives both inverse homotopies
Full all-dimensional groupoid construction in a precise higher model

intro.groupoids.mathematics: An infinity-groupoid is an infinity-category in which the 1-morphisms are also weakly invertible; the path example has this feature.
intro.groupoids.proof: Terminology for the intended higher setting; path reversal motivates invertibility.
intro.groupoids.plain: The extra condition concerns arrows between objects, since higher arrows were already weakly invertible.
intro.groupoids.story: Every route in Mira's path ledger has a reversible return up to deformation, as well as higher comparisons.
intro.groupoids.limit: A strict groupoid or the fundamental 1-groupoid records only a truncation, not the full infinity-groupoid.

intro.models.mathematics: Quasicategories and complete Segal spaces are cited as concrete approaches; the course proposes an axiomatic synthetic approach instead.
intro.models.proof: This is methodological context, with references rather than a theorem comparing models.
intro.models.plain: Different formal languages can present higher categories. The notes announce which approach the course will use.
intro.models.story: Mira compares different blueprints for describing a city before choosing a charter based on its structural behavior.
intro.models.limit: No equivalence of models is stated or proved in these pages.

intro.hott.mathematics: In the intended homotopy type theory, types carry terms and iterated identity types and behave as infinity-groupoids.
intro.hott.proof: This describes the intended foundations; those foundations are not Lean's proof-irrelevant equality theory.
intro.hott.plain: Identifications can carry information and can themselves be compared.
intro.hott.story: Mira records not only that two names identify the same object, but also which identification was chosen and how identifications compare.
intro.hott.limit: Replacing these identity types by Lean Eq erases the higher information and would not prove the stated claim.
obligations: Interpret types as infinity-groupoids in the intended homotopical foundations

intro.identity.mathematics: For x,y:X, an identity type x=y can have terms p,q, whose identifications form another identity type p=q, and this iteration continues.
intro.identity.proof: The passage describes the syntax and interpretation of homotopy type theory.
intro.identity.plain: The distinction is between saying that an equality holds and retaining structured identifications as objects of further study.
intro.identity.story: Mira keeps certificates of identification, then certificates comparing those certificates.
intro.identity.limit: Lean propositions are proof-irrelevant. Its iterated equality cannot be presented as the nontrivial higher identity structure of HoTT.

intro.sip.mathematics: Equality allows substitution of properties and transport of structures. The intended structure identity principle relates identities of groups to group isomorphisms. Existence of an element of order two is isomorphism-invariant; presentation-specific statements about the identity being the number 0 need not be. The source compares the cyclic group on {0,1} with the multiplicative group {1,−1}.
intro.sip.proof: Equality transport is available in ordinary dependent type theory. Group isomorphisms preserve multiplication, the identity and element order. The structure identity principle requires the intended univalent/homotopical setting.
intro.sip.plain: Ordinary equality supports substitution. Isomorphism preserves structural properties, but not every statement about how a structure was represented as sets.
intro.sip.story: Two clerks encode the same two-state group with different labels. An element of order two survives translation, while the printed name of the identity can change. Mira distinguishes a change of labels from a change of group structure.
intro.sip.limit: Group isomorphism is not automatically equality of Lean's bundled groups. A proof of order invariance does not prove the structure identity principle.
obligations: Group isomorphisms preserve existence of an element of order two
Explicit cyclic-two/sign-group isomorphism and different identity labels
Structure identity principle in the intended foundations

intro.synthetic.mathematics: The synthetic approach extends the intended type theory to include noninvertible morphisms and studies the structural behavior of categories axiomatically.
intro.synthetic.proof: The specific extended type theory and axioms are announced for later parts of the course.
intro.synthetic.plain: The opening describes a research language to be developed, not an already supplied Lean axiom system.
intro.synthetic.story: Mira plans a richer charter that can speak both of reversible identifications and of genuinely one-way permits.
intro.synthetic.limit: No new project axioms should be invented to make this informal announcement look checked.

intro.course.mathematics: Later course topics are announced: foundations, localisations, fibrations, Yoneda, Kan extensions, limits and colimits. Their general synthetic development is not part of this 13-page installment.
intro.course.proof: A syllabus announcement has no proof obligation.
intro.course.plain: These names indicate where the course is going. This learning project follows only the supplied installment.
intro.course.story: Mira reads the titles of future chapters before studying the route-book rules actually provided today.
intro.course.limit: Mentioning a later topic does not justify adding a separate formalization program for it here.

strict.motivation.mathematics: The source calls ordinary categories strict and motivates higher foundations partly by constructions that depend on equality of object presentations rather than equivalence.
strict.motivation.proof: Motivational context; the walking-isomorphism example later supplies a concrete distinction.
strict.motivation.plain: Literal object data can change even when two categories describe equivalent structure.
strict.motivation.story: Mira compares two differently labelled ledgers that encode the same pattern of permits.
strict.motivation.limit: This is not a theorem that every equality-sensitive construction is invalid; the specific invariance requirement must be stated.

equivalences.motivation.mathematics: Equality, isomorphism and equivalence of strict categories are distinct notions. The one-object category and walking isomorphism are equivalent despite having different numbers of objects.
equivalences.motivation.proof: The explicit functors and natural isomorphisms are given in items 3.8–3.9; the object sets have cardinalities one and two.
equivalences.motivation.plain: Equivalence permits redundant isomorphic objects. A strict isomorphism of categories would require inverse object functions.
equivalences.motivation.story: Mira's two-room ledger and one-room model have different numbers of names but equivalent permit structure.
equivalences.motivation.limit: The distinction concerns object presentations and categorical equivalence, not equality of the chosen object sets.
obligations: One-object category has object cardinality one
Walking isomorphism is not strictly isomorphic to the one-object category

3.5.adjoint_upgrade.mathematics: Every equivalence in the source's quasi-inverse sense can be promoted to an adjoint equivalence.
3.5.adjoint_upgrade.proof: The source cites this fact without using it. In ordinary category theory one can modify the unit or counit to obtain the triangle identities while retaining quasi-inverse functors.
3.5.adjoint_upgrade.plain: Arbitrary natural isomorphisms witnessing a quasi-inverse need not already satisfy the triangles. An upgrade supplies coherent choices.
3.5.adjoint_upgrade.story: Mira already has reversible round-trip comparisons. She adjusts the certificates so the two special triangle journeys agree with the neutral permits.
3.5.adjoint_upgrade.limit: Do not assume the original comparison isomorphisms already satisfy the triangle identities.
obligations: Upgrade arbitrary quasi-inverse natural isomorphisms to adjoint-equivalence data
